evidence.note: Three REAL governance proposals, analysed by Bradbury validators on this deployment. Each recomputes from its own stored evidence on chain: `genlayer call <addr> verify_assessment --args <id>` returns verified true with no differences.
evidence.composability_proof: GovernanceConsumer.preflight(<ENS proposal url>) returns would_release true with no blockers, reading assessment 3 across the contract boundary and applying its own snapshotted terms (RECOMMEND required, min_score 70). strict_release(3) is require_recommended reached across the boundary and returns the record; strict_release(2) reverts with `[EXPECTED] assessment 2 ([Constitutional] AIP Fast Feed) is CAUTION at 50/100; flags: UNSTATED_AMOUNT,PLACEHOLDER_TERMS,NO_CLAWBACK,NO_REFERENCES`. All three re-run against 0x7f5d0a398ea506BcfACE622a7139a4c0190E061b.
evidence.tally_on_bradbury: NOT analysed on Bradbury. The Tally path IS proven on Studionet — the live suite assessed www.tally.xyz/gov/uniswap/proposal/86 successfully as part of its 97 passing checks — but every Bradbury attempt during this session hit the node's gas-rate limit ("node is at capacity") and the 225 KB page makes it the heaviest of the three fetches. Recorded as not done rather than described as done.
evidence.network_conditions: Bradbury was congested throughout: `transaction gas rate limit exceeded: node is at capacity, retry in ~858ms` on most submissions, and one round reported LEADER_TIMEOUT and then settled anyway after rotation. The CLI's exit status is not a reliable signal on this network; the contract's own state is.

tagline: Every proposal deserves a second opinion.
summary: An on-chain risk oracle for DAO governance proposals. Submit any Snapshot, Tally or Discourse-forum proposal URL; five GenLayer validators independently fetch the proposal, apply one fixed rubric, and agree on an assessment across five dimensions (feasibility 25, budget 25, centralization 20, clarity 15, alignment 15). Nineteen features are parsed from the immutable proposal text and five come from a model that must quote the proposal verbatim and is clamped into bounds the parser computed. The verdict is derived by arithmetic, never asked of a model. Every stored number recomputes from the evidence beside it, and any contract can gate on it with require_recommended().

consensus.parsed_fields: 19 ordinals parsed from the proposal text — exact equality, no tolerance. The body is signed and pinned, so a disagreement means one node read a different document.
consensus.model_fields: 5 ladder levels — three independent checks: the leader's quote verifies verbatim (28+ contiguous characters) against the text THIS node fetched; the level sits inside the bounds THIS node computed; and it is within one rung of THIS node's own reading.
consensus.why: docs/PROBE.md section 5. Five validators asked for five free ordinals settled 0 rounds of 3. A single three-valued verdict settled 0 of 4. Median-of-3 per node settled 0 of 4. An explicit ladder alone settled 0 of 5. The ladder PLUS a normalised quote gate PLUS parser bounds is what settles.
consensus.disclosed_tolerance: Two accepted readings of one proposal can differ by one rung on a dimension. Published in get_config, on /docs, and made observable by get_assessment_history. Bradbury scored the Aave proposal RECOMMEND 75 where Studionet scored it CAUTION 60 — the same rubric, two independent validator sets.
consensus.verdict: Derived deterministically from the five dimensions. Any dimension at its worst rung forfeits a RECOMMEND; two of them is an OPPOSE whatever the average says; three model abstentions forfeit it too.

data_sources.snapshot: hub.snapshot.org/graphql — the proposal body is signed and IPFS-pinned; the CID is stored as an anchor
data_sources.tally: www.tally.xyz/gov/<org>/proposal/<n> — read from the page's own __NEXT_DATA__ payload; api.tally.xyz returns 401 without a key, which a contract cannot hold
data_sources.discourse: any forum running Discourse, via /t/<id>.json — the slug is ignored by Discourse itself and is discarded
data_sources.never_fetched: the submitted URL. snapshot.org/#/<space>/proposal/<0x…> answers 200 with a 1,363-byte empty app shell, byte-identical for every proposal that has ever existed.
data_sources.never_read: scores, scores_total, votes and state are excluded from the request the validators make, not merely ignored afterwards
